findings.title: Global group canManage incorrectly accepts view scope
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() the fallback check is hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) on the all-groups resource, identical to canView(). This means an admin with only the view scope on Groups passes requireManage(), which guards create top-level group, delete and other manage operations. A view-only delegated admin can therefore create, update and delete groups, which is a privilege escalation.

findings.title: Group view permission scan uses resource ID instead of group ID
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the code iterates resources of type Groups and calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...) and granted.add(groupResource.getId()). For admin permissions, resource name equals the group ID and resource ID is a generated UUID. The lookup must use getName(), as V1 does with getName().substring(prefix). Using getId() means the per-group evaluation looks up a non-existent resource and the returned set contains authz UUIDs instead of group IDs, so user search filtered by UserModel.GROUPS returns empty or wrong results for group-scoped admins.

findings.title: Per-group check shadows all-groups permission
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission loads resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) and only if it is null falls back to the all-groups resource. If a per-group resource exists at all, for example created for a different admin, the all-groups permission is never evaluated. An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all groups is then denied for that specific group despite the all-groups grant. The same pattern exists for users, breaking the expected all-users/all-groups transitive semantics.

findings.title: Per-user check shadows all-users permission
findings.body: UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission loads resourceStore.findByName(server, user.getId()) and only if null falls back to the all-users resource. If a per-user resource exists for the target user, for example created for another admin, the all-users permission is never evaluated. An admin with MANAGE or VIEW on all users loses access to that user, so creating any single-user permission revokes all-users access for other admins.

findings.title: Missing null check for all-groups resource causes NPE on upgrade
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission falls back to AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource for Groups and immediately calls policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) without checking for null. Realms upgraded from before Groups existed, or realms where the resource server is not fully initialized, have no Groups type resource, so resource is null and the call throws NullPointerException, crashing every group permission check. UserPermissionsV2 line 111 has the same unchecked pattern.

findings.title: Scope deduplication via Set does not work
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init collects new ScopeRepresentation objects into a Set to get rid of duplicities, but ScopeRepresentation does not implement equals/hashCode so each new instance is distinct. Scopes like manage and view that appear in Clients, Groups and Users types remain duplicated in the list passed to RepresentationToModel.toModel, causing duplicate scope creation attempts or failures when first enabling admin permissions.

findings.title: getScope NPE on unknown resource type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getScope does SCHEMA.getResourceTypes().get(resourceType).getScopes() without checking that resourceType exists. A null or unknown resourceType causes NullPointerException instead of ModelValidationException, turning a bad admin API request into a 500 error.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle Groups type
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceName only special-cases Users, returning All users or the username, and otherwise returns resource.getDisplayName(). Group resources store the group ID as name with no displayName, so group permissions resolve to null or blank names in the admin UI and APIs. The new Groups type needs an All groups case and group name resolution like users.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc references wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws if canManageMembership returns false, duplicating the comment on requireManageMembership. It should reference canManageMembers. Readers cannot tell which check is enforced without reading the implementation.
